thread:
marta: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel selector change I see a 2.8x P99 on the embed->rerank path for a subset of tenants. repro attached to this thread.
cheng: is this from synthetic load or the replay harness?
marta: replay harness. synthetic didn't show as bad. replay uses last-week production traces, same client payloads.
perf-bot: benchmark job 1781234567 queued (embed-rerank, vectors=1536, payload=~3kb, workers=16).
samir: can you paste the run cmd & the p95/p99 numbers?
marta: run command:```./replay_harness --trace=2026-03-10 --endpoint=embed-rerank --batcher=auto --kernels=auto --workers=16 --concurrency=128```
marta: baseline (old kernel selector): p50=23ms p95=120ms p99=210ms
marta: after change: p50=26ms p95=240ms p99=590ms
elaine: huge. are KV cache miss rates higher in replay?
marta: yes — replay has more cold prefixes. metric shows KV cache hit drop from 89%->61% for that tenant.
cheng: kernel selector may have picked a different matmul kernel optimized for large batch steady-state but with higher setup cost per new KV context. that aligns with cold-prefix tail.
samir: can we confirm with perf profile? small flamegraph or nvprof snapshot?
marta: attached a quick flame snippet: top contributors are: kernel_launch_overhead, cuMemcpyAsync stalls, and a few custom attention kernels with high variance.
elaine: interesting — batching heuristics changed too around the same time, right? auto-batcher now prefers larger batches up to 64 based on latency headroom.
marta: yes. replay traffic has many small queries that get artificially coalesced into 32-64 batches in the new heuristic. that increases per-request KV cache pressure and evictions.
cheng: so two interacting effects: (1) kernel swap with higher kernel_launch setup cost, (2) larger batches increasing KV working set & evictions. both amplify tail.
samir: quick experiment suggestion: force old kernel + new batcher, and new kernel + old batcher. narrow which axis has the dominant effect.
marta: I ran both: old kernel + new batcher: p99=260ms (bad but not 590). new kernel + old batcher: p99=240ms. combination is worst -> suggests nonlinear interaction.
perf-bot: artifacts uploaded: /artifacts/1781234567/{flame.svg,kv-metrics.csv,raw-trace.pb}
cheng: thanks. initial mitigation options: 1) revert kernel selector change, 2) change batcher cap for replay tenant (max_batch=16), 3) tune KV cache sizing or per-tenant pinning.
elaine: for a short-term rollback I'd prefer cap batching to 16 for affected tenants + increase KV cache for that pool. rollback of kernel selector is riskier for other workloads.
samir: agree. also add a canary with replay harness (10% traffic) using the new kernel + tuned batcher to validate.
marta: I'll open a short issue with steps and perf numbers, and enqueue a canary for tomorrow 0300 UTC.
cheng: also add a synthetic case that mimics cold-prefix heavy workloads (many short unique prefixes) so we catch regressions earlier in CI.
elaine: good call. small test plan: reproduce, mitigation (cap batcher + bump cache), canary, rollback plan if canary fails.
marta: I'll post the issue link here once created. thx everyone. :thumbsup:
